canonical_statement: The minireview aims to summarize available data and outline the authors' approach to anticoagulation for cancer-associated VTE with thrombocytopenia.
The optimal anticoagulation approach for patients with cancer-associated VTE and thrombocytopenia is not established.
Thrombocytopenia is not protective against thrombosis and is associated with increased bleeding risk, particularly during anticoagulation.
Patients with thrombocytopenia are often excluded from randomized anticoagulation trials, limiting evidence for treatment decisions in this population.
Approximately one quarter of 3,635 cancer-associated thrombosis events occurred in the setting of thrombocytopenia.

canonical_statement: Approximately one in ten of 3,635 cancer-associated thrombosis events occurred with platelet counts below 50,000/µL.

At 60 days in TROVE, major bleeding with full-dose anticoagulation was 12.8% (95% CI 4.9%-20.8%).

canonical_statement: Large randomized studies establishing direct oral anticoagulants for cancer-associated thrombosis excluded patients with significant thrombocytopenia.
In TROVE, 3 of 16 patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants developed clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

population.label: TROVE patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants

canonical_statement: Heparin (LMWH or unfractionated heparin) is commonly used for cancer-associated thrombosis with thrombocytopenia because its shorter half-life permits dose modification and it has relatively few drug interactions.

Kopolovic et al (2015) was summarized as a single-center retrospective cohort of 74 hospitalized patients with cancer-associated thrombosis and thrombocytopenia; 23% received no therapy, 40.5% full-dose anticoagulation, and 36.5% partial treatment.

For Kopolovic et al (2015), Table 1 reports recurrent VTE in 31.1%, bleeding events in 17.6%, and major bleeding in 4.1%; the displayed event counts do not mathematically align with the displayed percentages.

In the Hokusai VTE Cancer dalteparin arm (N=524), dalteparin was held for platelets <50,000/µL and dose-reduced for platelets 50,000-100,000/µL; dose reduction was prespecified but not tested as a trial question.
In the Hokusai VTE Cancer dalteparin arm, 10% (53/524) developed platelet counts below 100,000/µL and 2% (10/524) had platelet counts below 50,000/µL during the study.

population.label: Dalteparin arm of Hokusai VTE Cancer

canonical_statement: In the Caravaggio dalteparin arm (N=579), dalteparin was held for platelets <50,000/µL and dose-reduced for platelets 50,000-100,000/µL according to the dalteparin package insert; this dose-reduction strategy was not a trial question.
In the Caravaggio dalteparin arm, thrombocytopenia was reported in 2.9% (17/579) of patients.

population.label: Dalteparin arm of Caravaggio

canonical_statement: Holding anticoagulation may be appropriate for selected patients with low thrombotic burden, reversible thrombosis causes, or extremely high bleeding risk.
When anticoagulation is withheld, decisions should incorporate patient values and goals of care and patients should be closely monitored for thrombosis progression or changing bleeding risk.

Inferior vena cava filter use in active malignancy should be limited because of higher complication rates and lower retrieval rates; anticoagulation after filter placement should be considered to reduce filter-associated complications.
Recommendation: for cancer-associated thrombosis with platelet count ≥50,000/µL, give full therapeutic anticoagulation without platelet transfusion (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Patients with cancer-associated thrombosis and platelet count ≥50,000/µL

concept.text: Full therapeutic anticoagulation without platelet transfusion

canonical_statement: Recommendation: for acute cancer-associated thrombosis with platelets <50,000/µL and large-burden PE, use full-dose LMWH or unfractionated heparin with platelet-transfusion support to maintain 40,000-50,000/µL (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Acute CAT with severe thrombocytopenia and large-burden pulmonary embolism
inclusion_criteria: Large-burden PE such as submassive PE, heart strain, or central pulmonary artery involvement

concept.text: Full-dose LMWH or unfractionated heparin with platelet transfusion support

canonical_statement: Recommendation: for acute CAT with platelets <50,000/µL and proximal lower-extremity DVT or segmental PE, use either full-dose LMWH with higher platelet targets or dose-modified LMWH; beyond 30 days after acute VTE, favor dose-modified LMWH (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Acute CAT with severe thrombocytopenia and proximal lower-extremity DVT or segmental PE

concept.text: Full-dose LMWH with higher platelet targets

canonical_statement: Recommendation: for lower-risk acute CAT with platelet count 25,000-50,000/µL, reduce LMWH to 50% of the therapeutic dose or use prophylactic-dose LMWH (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Lower-risk acute CAT with platelet count 25,000-50,000/µL
inclusion_criteria: Distal lower-extremity DVT, isolated subsegmental PE, or catheter-related thrombosis

concept.text: LMWH at 50% therapeutic dose or prophylactic dose

canonical_statement: Recommendation: for lower-risk acute CAT while platelets are <25,000/µL, temporarily discontinue anticoagulation; during the first 2 weeks after thrombosis, favor transfusion to 25,000/µL plus lower-dose anticoagulation (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Lower-risk acute CAT with platelet count <25,000/µL
inclusion_criteria: Distal lower-extremity DVT, isolated subsegmental PE, or catheter-related thrombosis

concept.text: Platelet transfusion to 25,000/µL with lower-dose anticoagulation during first 2 weeks

canonical_statement: Recommendation: resume full-dose LMWH when platelet count is >50,000/µL without transfusion support and no other contraindication is present (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Patients with CAT after thrombocytopenia improves above 50,000/µL without transfusion support

canonical_statement: Recommendation: for patients at high risk of hemorrhage or with active hemorrhage, observation without anticoagulation may be considered, with consideration of inferior vena cava filter placement (certainty of evidence: Very Low +).

population.label: Patients with CAT at high risk of hemorrhage or with active hemorrhage
